The row exists for the CLASS, not for a wound. 🔍 **WHY THE INSTRUCTION WAS WRONG, precisely, because "be careful" is not a cure:** it silently assumed a re-home is a DISCONTINUITY — a new destination starting an empty series. A re-home is a MOVE. The author conflated *"the directory changed"* with *"the coverage changed"*, and only the second is what the anchor declares. 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is a new axis beside [[a-span-guard-calls-a-lost-series-whole]]: an external denominator is only as good as the RULE FOR UPDATING IT, and that rule is consumed at exactly the moment its author is not there to re-derive it.** A maintenance instruction is CODE WITH NO TEST AND NO READER-CHECK: nothing executes it, nothing reds when it is wrong, and it is obeyed under time pressure by the one person doing the very migration it describes. **How to apply: when you write "edit this file when X happens", write the PREDICATE that makes the edit correct, not the EVENT that prompts it** — here, "edit it when the series' first covered DAY changes; a move that carries every file across is not such a change" — and where you can, make the wrong edit red a guard rather than a reader. 🔧 **CURED IN THE SAME COMMIT:** `whenToEditThis` now states the predicate, names this non-change as its worked example, and the `history` array carries the re-home as a deliberate UNCHANGED entry, so the next reader can see the question was asked and answered rather than skipped.
